t: Bring your calendar, contacts and records from another app
s: Import a calendar file, contacts and past records on the web. Files are kept exactly as they are, marked as imported.
k: import switch ourfamilywizard talkingparents appclose cozi 2houses ics vcf
x: On the web, Import from another app brings what you already have into Clearly. Open it from Settings, then Import from another app, then Start an import, or from the Records page. Choose where you're coming from: OurFamilyWizard, TalkingParents, AppClose, Cozi, 2houses or something else. Clearly shows where to look for that app's export option. Menus change between versions, so look for "export" or "download" in its settings. Calendar Export your calendar from the other app as an .ics file (up to 5 MB). Upload it. Clearly reads events from 3 years back to 1 year ahead. Repeating events stay a series. Choose whether to Include past events and which kid they're for. Click to add them. Events already in Clearly with the same date and name are skipped. Each imported event notes which file it came from. Your co-parent is told. Contacts Upload a .vcf file, choose a type for each contact (doctor, school, and so on) and add them. Contacts already in Clearly with the same name are skipped. Past messages and records Upload a PDF, image, CSV, text or Word file, up to 25 MB. Give it a name, say where it's from and what dates it covers. Clearly keeps the file exactly as it is, marked as imported. It isn't turned into Clearly messages. See Imported records. Note: Kids and the custody schedule aren't imported. Set those up under Shared. Importing needs a subscription, and nothing is saved until you confirm.

s: Sign up on the web or in the iPhone app with your name, email and a password.
k: sign up register new account password rules confirm email
x: If your co-parent already uses Clearly, ask them for an invite link or code first and follow Join your co-parent's family instead. Joining is free. On the web Go to web.getclearly.app/signup. Enter your First name, Last name, Email and Password. Tick I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy. Click Create account. In the iPhone app Open Clearly and tap Get started. Enter your First name, Last name, Email and Create a password. Tap Create account. Password rules Your password needs at least 8 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a number. Clearly also turns down passwords that have appeared in a known data breach, because they are easy to guess. Only a short, scrambled piece of the password is checked; the password itself is never sent anywhere. Confirming your email If you're asked to confirm your email, open the message from Clearly and tap the link, then sign in. If it doesn't arrive within a few minutes, check your spam or junk folder. Note: There is no Sign in with Apple or Google. You sign in with your email and password, on the web and iPhone alike. Tip: Use the same email on the web and in the iPhone app. It's one account, so everything you do in one shows up in the other.

s: Send an invite by email, by text or any app, or share your family code. Your subscription covers them.
k: invite co-parent family code invite link resend cancel invite
x: Inviting your co-parent needs a subscription, and that subscription covers them too. They never pay to join. On the web On Today, find Invite your co-parent, or go to Settings and then Co-parent. To have Clearly send it, enter Their email and click Send invite. To send it yourself, use Copy invite, Text it (on a phone) or Share…, or copy your Family code. Clearly reminds them after 3 days, and again the day before the invite expires. An emailed invite lasts 30 days. While an invite is waiting you can Resend, Change email or Cancel invite. Only one emailed invite can be waiting at a time. Your family code keeps working even if you cancel an emailed invite. In the iPhone app On Today, tap Invite, or open Settings (your initial at the top right) and go to Co-parent. Choose Text, Email or Another app, or tap Invite code to copy it. What they get The invite contains a link like getclearly.app/join/ABC234 and your 6-character family code. Tapping the link on their phone opens Clearly with the code filled in. They can also enter the code by hand. See Join your co-parent's family. When they join, you're told, and Settings shows you as connected. Note: A family has two parents at most. If your co-parent left Clearly, you can invite someone again.

s: Use the link or 6-character code your co-parent sent. Joining is free, and you get their setup straight away.
k: join invite code family code link connect co-parent already on clearly
x: Joining is free. Your co-parent's subscription covers you both. With the link Tap the link in the invite on your phone, or open it on a computer. Create your account. The code is remembered, so you don't have to type it. Clearly connects you to the family when you finish. With the code On the web: create your account at web.getclearly.app/signup, choose Yes, or I have a code, enter the code and click Continue. On iPhone: on the first screen tap I have an invite code, enter the code, tap Continue, then create your account. Family codes are 6 characters and never use the letters I or O or the numbers 0 or 1, so there's nothing to mix up. If you already set up on your own On iPhone: open Settings, go to Co-parent and tap Join with their code, or tap your co-parent's link. Clearly asks you to confirm, because the schedule and children you set up on your own will no longer be shown. You'll use the family your co-parent set up. What you see after joining You get the kids, schedule, holidays, summer and expense split your co-parent set up. Either of you can change them under Shared. If the code doesn't work, see My invite code doesn't work.

s: Add your kids, set the custody schedule, holidays and summer, and agree the expense split. It takes about five minutes.
k: setup onboarding family name children getting started checklist
x: The parent who starts on Clearly sets up the family. The co-parent who joins later uses the same setup and can change it afterwards. On the web After you create your account, Clearly asks whether your co-parent has already started. Choose No, I'm starting. Name your family if you like. Leave it empty and Clearly uses both parents' names. Start your free trial now, or choose Skip for now and set things up first. On Today, the Set up your family card lists the steps: - Add your kids - Set the custody schedule - Choose your holidays (or Not needed) - Set the summer schedule (or Not needed) - Agree the expense split - Invite your co-parent Each step opens the right page under Shared in the sidebar. In the iPhone app On Getting started, choose Start fresh. Your children: add each child's first name and birthdate. A family name is optional. Custody schedule: pick a pattern, say who starts, check the preview and set the exchange time. Summer: choose No, same all year or Yes, summer is different. Holiday schedule: pick the holidays you alternate. Shared expenses: set how you split costs for the kids. All set: check the summary, then continue to start your trial and invite your co-parent. Change it later Everything you set up can be changed. On the web, use Shared in the sidebar. On iPhone, use the Shared tab. Either parent can make changes. Note: Setting up is free. Inviting your co-parent, posting and logging need a subscription. One covers you both. See What works without a subscription.

t: Try the demo before you sign up
s: The iPhone app has a 14-day demo with a simulated co-parent. No account needed, and nothing is saved.
k: demo try virtual co-parent no account jordan alex
x: The demo lets you try Clearly with a simulated co-parent before you create an account. Start the demo Open the Clearly app. Tap Try it with a virtual co‑parent. Read how Clearly uses AI and tap Agree and continue. A short tour starts. You are "Alex", and "Jordan" is the simulated co-parent, who replies a few seconds after you do. Demo replies are marked Demo · simulated co-parent. What you can't do in the demo Export records Add photos to replies Invite professionals Join a real family or subscribe Leave the demo Tap Start free to create your real account. Tap Leave demo to clear the demo. Anything you added in the demo is removed. The demo lasts 14 days on your phone. When it ends you can restart it or exit. Note: The demo is in the iPhone app only. On the web, you start with a real account.

t: Use a plan code from the plan builder
s: A code from the free custody plan builder sets up your family with the schedule, holidays and split you chose.
k: plan builder plan code custody plan import plan
x: If you made a plan with the free custody plan builder, it gave you a code. That code sets up your family in Clearly with what you chose. Create your account at web.getclearly.app/signup. When Clearly asks whether your co-parent has already started, choose Yes, or I have a code. Enter your plan code and click Continue. Clearly creates your family with the schedule, holidays, summer, expense split, kids and payment method from your plan. You can change any of it under Shared. If the code doesn't match, Clearly says so. Check it and try again. After several wrong codes you have to wait an hour.

t: What Clearly is and how the pieces fit
s: Clearly is a co-parenting app for two parents, on the web and iPhone, with a free read-only portal for the professionals they choose.
k: overview about android browser iphone professional portal
x: Clearly gives two co-parents one shared place for messages, the custody schedule, shared expenses and the parenting plan. Everything you post stays on the record exactly as written, with times recorded by the server. Three ways in Clearly on the web at web.getclearly.app. Works in any current browser on a computer, an Android phone, an iPad or a tablet. The iPhone app, from the App Store. It is a companion to the web app: same account, same record. The professional portal at web.getclearly.app/pro, a free, read-only view for the lawyer, mediator, therapist or parenting coordinator a parent invites. You and your co-parent can use different ones. One of you can be on an Android phone and the other on iPhone. What's in it Topics. Each conversation is a topic that ends in an answer or a resolution you both accept. See How topics work. Schedule. Your custody pattern, holidays, summer, events and swap requests. See Set up your custody schedule. Expenses. Log a shared cost, split it, attach a receipt and settle up. See Log an expense. Shared. Kids, health details, contacts and the parts of your parenting plan you both see. Records. PDFs and spreadsheets of your record, each PDF with a document ID anyone can check. See Export your record. Professionals. Give the professional you work with a read-only view of the areas you choose. See Invite a professional. What it costs One subscription covers both parents, on the web and iPhone. Reading, searching and exporting your record are always free. Professionals never pay. See Plans and prices.

t: Check your app version and update
s: Find your version at the bottom of Settings, and update from the App Store.
k: version update update required old version
x: Find your version Open Settings in Clearly and scroll to the bottom. You'll see a line like "Clearly v2.0.7 (35)". Update Open the App Store. Tap your profile picture at the top right. Find Clearly under updates and tap Update. To update automatically, open the iPhone Settings app, tap App Store and turn on App Updates. "Update Clearly" screen If Clearly shows Update Clearly, that version is no longer supported. Tap Update to open the App Store. Nothing you've recorded is lost.

t: Find your way around the iPhone app
s: The five tabs, Settings, and what the red badges mean.
k: tabs navigation today badge settings quick actions tour
x: The tabs Today: who has the kids, the next exchange, what needs you, and what's coming up. Topics: your conversations. See How topics work. Schedule: the calendar, swap requests and holidays. Expenses: what's unpaid and what's paid. Shared: your plan, kids and contacts. Badges A red number on a tab means something is waiting on you: topics to read or answer, swap requests to answer, or expenses you owe. The app icon shows the total. Settings Tap your initial in the circle at the top right of any tab. See iPhone settings. Quick actions On Today, the buttons for a swap request, a new expense, a new event and a new topic save a few taps. Choose which ones show in Settings, then Quick actions. Take the tour again Open Settings and tap Take the tour.

s: Get Clearly from the App Store and sign in with the same account you use on the web.
k: download app store install ipad iphone ios
x: On your iPhone, open the Clearly page in the App Store. Tap Get. Open Clearly. Tap Sign in if you already have an account, or Get started to create one. If you already use Clearly on the web, sign in with the same email and password. Your record, schedule and subscription are all there. Note: The app is for iPhone. On an Android phone, an iPad or a computer, use Clearly on the web, which has the same record.

s: Turn phone notifications on or off in iOS Settings, and choose which emails Clearly sends.
k: push notifications alerts badge turn off email
x: Clearly asks to send notifications once, after setup. You can change your answer at any time. Turn phone notifications on or off Open the iPhone Settings app. Scroll down and tap Clearly. Tap Notifications and turn Allow Notifications on or off. In Clearly you can also go to Settings, then Email notifications, then Phone notifications, which opens the same place. What you're notified about Topics: a new topic, a question, an FYI, a reply, an answer, a proposed resolution, and when a topic is resolved or goes back to talking. Schedule: a swap request, an accepted or declined swap, a removed swap, and a new event. Expenses: a new expense, and an expense marked paid. Tap a notification to open the thing it's about. Emails Emails are set separately. See Email notifications.

s: What's in Settings, from your profile and subscription to the color theme and export.
k: settings profile preferences reframing style color theme export help version
x: Tap your initial at the top right of any tab to open Settings. Profile card: tap it to edit your display name and email, change your password, sign out or delete your account. Subscription: your plan, who pays, and Manage subscription. Also whether the cost is shared through Expenses. Family: the family name, which professionals you invite also see. Co-parent: your invite code, invite by email, or join with their code. Professionals: invite a professional and see who has access. Calendar sharing: your calendar link. See Subscribe to your calendar. Preferences: - Reimbursement: how you get paid back for expenses. - Email notifications - Reframing style: the default style when Clearly suggests wording (Brief, Balanced or Warm). - Color theme: only on this phone. - Quick actions on Today. - Take the tour Support: Send feedback, Export data, Help, and the privacy policy and terms. The version number is at the bottom, for example "Clearly v2.0.7 (35)".

s: Start your trial or subscribe through Apple, restore a purchase, or, in the US, subscribe on the web from the plans screen.
k: paywall apple in-app purchase restore purchases subscribe on the web upgrade to annual
x: Subscribe through Apple Open the plans screen. It appears when you invite your co-parent or try to post, and from the subscription card on Today. Choose Annual or Monthly. Tap Start free trial, or Start annual or Start monthly if you've had a trial before. Confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your Apple ID password. The prices shown come from the App Store in your country. Subscribe on the web instead (US) In the US App Store, the plans screen also shows Or subscribe on the web, at web.getclearly.app. Tapping it opens Safari already signed in to your account. Once you've paid, Clearly sends you back to the app, where your subscription is active. This needs version 2.0.7 or later. If your co-parent already pays The plans screen shows Your family is covered. There's nothing to buy. Restore a purchase If you reinstalled the app or changed phones, open the plans screen and tap Restore purchases. Switch from monthly to annual Open Settings, tap your subscription, then Manage subscription and Upgrade to annual. Note: The app doesn't take offer codes. If a professional gave you an App Store code, redeem it in the App Store app. See A free month from a professional.

s: Choose emails for topics, the schedule and expenses. Emails say what happened, never what anyone wrote.
k: email notifications turn off emails unsubscribe alerts
x: Change your emails On the web: go to Settings, then Email notifications. On iPhone: open Settings, then Email notifications. Turn Email me on or off, and choose Topics and replies, Schedule and Expenses. It's one setting, so a change on the web also applies on iPhone. What's in them An email tells you what happened, for example that your co-parent replied in a topic, and links to it. It never includes what anyone wrote. You get at most one email per topic every 30 minutes. Emails you always get Clearly always emails you when your co-parent joins, and when professional access to your record changes.

t: Find your way around the web app
s: The sidebar, the Today page, the setup card and the tour.
k: sidebar menu today navigation tour shared record
x: The sidebar Today: who has the kids, the next exchange, what needs you, and what's coming up. Topics: your conversations. Schedule: the calendar, events and swap requests. Expenses: what's owed and what's settled. Shared: Kids, Contacts, Custody schedule, Shared expenses (the split) and Calendar sharing. Record: Records (exports) and Professionals. Settings, at the bottom, with your name and whether your co-parent has joined. Numbers next to Today, Topics and Expenses show what's waiting on you. On a phone, tap the menu button at the top left to open the sidebar. A dot on it means something needs you. Today Custody card: who has the kids today, the next exchange, and the next 14 days. For you: topics, expenses and swap requests waiting on you. Coming up: the next five events. The setup card Until setup is done, Set up your family on Today shows the steps left. See Set up your family. The tour The tour runs once in each browser. To see it again, go to Settings, then Appearance, then Take the tour. If it doesn't start, reload the page.

s: Sign in at web.getclearly.app in any current browser, on a computer, Android phone, iPad or tablet.
k: browser web app chrome safari edge firefox computer laptop
x: Clearly on the web is the full app in a browser. It's the same account and the same record as the iPhone app. Go to web.getclearly.app. Sign in with your email and password, or click Create an account. It works in current versions of Chrome, Safari, Edge and Firefox. Keep your browser up to date. On a shared computer Click Settings, then Account, then Sign out when you're done. Your appearance choice and a few display preferences are remembered per browser. When Clearly updates If you see Clearly has been updated., click Refresh to get the new version. Nothing you saved is lost.

s: Search topics, messages, the schedule, expenses, kids and contacts at once.
k: search find command k ctrl k keyword
x: On the web Press ⌘K on a Mac or Ctrl+K on Windows, or click Search in the sidebar. Type at least 2 characters. Try a word like "dentist" or "summer camp", a name, or an amount like "45". Use the arrow keys and press Enter to open a result, or click it. Results are grouped into Topics (including the text of messages), Schedule, Expenses and Shared. On iPhone On Topics, use the search box at the top. You can search for words, or ask a question such as what was resolved about pickups, and tap Ask Clearly.

t: Use Clearly on an Android phone
s: There's no Android app to install. Clearly on the web works in Chrome on any Android phone.
k: android samsung pixel google play home screen
x: Clearly doesn't have an app in Google Play. On Android, use Clearly on the web. It has everything your co-parent has on iPhone, on the same record. Open Chrome and go to web.getclearly.app. Sign in, or create your account. If your co-parent sent you an invite link, tap it first. Put it on your home screen In Chrome, tap the menu (three dots). Tap Add to Home screen or Install app. Clearly then opens from its own icon. Staying up to date Clearly on the web doesn't send phone notifications. Turn on emails instead, so you know when something needs you. See Email notifications.

t: Can messages be edited or deleted?
s: No. Topics, replies and answers stay exactly as written, with times recorded by the server.
k: edit message delete message unsend record permanent timestamps
x: No one can edit or delete a topic, reply or answer once it's posted: not you, not your co-parent, and not Clearly. Times are recorded by Clearly's server, not by your phone or computer. That's what makes the record dependable for both of you, and for anyone you share it with. What you can do Before you post, read it through. Clearly also checks each message, and suggests other wording when one is likely to make things harder. See When Clearly holds a message. After you post, add a reply to correct or explain something. If you started a topic by mistake, close or withdraw it. It stays on the record as no longer needed. See Close or withdraw a topic. If a parent deletes their account If your co-parent deletes their account, what they posted stays in your record, shown as "Former co-parent". See When a co-parent leaves Clearly.

t: Close or withdraw a topic you started
s: If you started a topic and it's sorted or no longer needed, you can close it. It stays on the record.
k: close topic withdraw sorted no longer needed cancel topic
x: On iPhone You can close a topic you started until your co-parent replies. Open the topic and tap ••• at the top right, then Close topic. Choose Sorted or No longer needed. On the web Open the topic you started. In the side panel, click Withdraw topic and confirm. Either way, the topic stays on the record and your co-parent is told. Once your co-parent has replied, a topic ends with a resolution you both accept, or closes on its own after 30 quiet days.

s: AI helps word messages, sums up where a topic stands and suggests resolutions, based on what you write. You decide what's posted.
k: ai anthropic claude privacy rewrite suggestions training
x: Clearly uses AI from Anthropic for a few jobs: Working out what kind of topic you're starting and giving it a title. Checking each message before your co-parent sees it, and suggesting other wording when one is likely to make things harder. Suggesting wording, drafting a reply and suggesting a resolution. Summing up where a conversation stands. Everything it suggests is based on what you and your co-parent wrote. It doesn't decide anything for you. You choose what's posted, and you can always write your own words instead. Your information What you write in topics, replies and answers is sent to Anthropic to provide these features. Anthropic doesn't use it to train its models. The AI never sees your photos or receipts. See the privacy policy for details. The iPhone app asks you to agree to this once, when you first sign in.

s: Every conversation is a topic about one thing, and it ends in an answer or a resolution you both accept.
k: topics messages conversation threads status open closed fyi question
x: In Clearly you don't send loose messages. You start a topic about one thing, such as a pickup time, a school form or a doctor's visit, and it stays together until it's settled. Kinds of topic When you write a topic, Clearly works out how your co-parent can answer it, based on what you wrote: A quick question they can answer Yes or No in one tap. A question they answer in a few words. An FYI they mark as seen. A conversation, for anything that needs back and forth. To send it another way, change the wording. Statuses Each topic shows where it is, for example: Waiting for you or Waiting for co-parent Resolution pending: one of you proposed how it ends. Resolved Closed · not accepted, Closed · no reply or Closed · no activity No longer needed Open and closed On iPhone, Topics has Open and Closed tabs. On the web, filter by Open, For you, Closed or All. A closed topic stays on the record. To raise it again, start a new topic.

s: When a topic is ready to end, one of you proposes how, and the other agrees or says not yet.
k: resolution propose agree resolve not yet undo where this stands settled agreement
x: A conversation ends with a resolution you both accept. It goes on the record as what you agreed. On iPhone When a conversation is ready, Clearly may offer a Suggested resolution, written from what you've both said. Tap Propose to send it, or Edit to write your own version first. Your co-parent sees Your co-parent proposed this, with Resolve and Not yet. While you wait, you see Waiting on your co-parent. Tap Undo to take your proposal back. Your co-parent is told. If your co-parent taps Not yet, the topic goes back to talking and you're told it's not settled yet. A new reply from either of you also sets a proposal aside. On the web In the topic's side panel, under Wrap it up, click Propose a resolution, write how it ends and click Propose. Your co-parent sees Agree and resolve and Propose something different. Where this stands On iPhone, Where this stands at the top of a conversation sums up what's settled and where each of you is, based on the conversation. Tap Ask for an update to refresh it. After it's resolved If the resolution includes a date or a cost, the iPhone app can offer Add to calendar or Add as expense. A proposal that isn't accepted within 30 days closes as Closed · not accepted. See When topics close on their own.

t: See whether your co-parent has read a topic
s: Clearly shows when a topic was delivered and when your co-parent opened it.
k: read receipts seen delivered opened check marks
x: On iPhone: one check mark means sent. Two check marks mean your co-parent has opened the topic. On the web: messages show Read with the time, or Delivered · not read yet. In a topic's side panel, Read by shows when each of you last opened it. Read receipts are always on, for both of you.

s: Answer a question in one tap, mark an FYI as seen, or write a reply. On iPhone you can add a photo.
k: reply answer yes no ok seen photo attachment draft a reply
x: Quick answers A quick question shows Yes and No. A question that needs a few words shows a box for your answer. An FYI shows OK on iPhone or OK, seen on the web. Once either of you writes a reply, the topic becomes a conversation and the one-tap buttons go away. Write a reply On iPhone: type in the Reply… box and tap Send. Tap the expand icon for a bigger box. With an empty box, Draft a reply suggests one based on the conversation. On the web: type in the box and click send, or press ⌘+Enter (Ctrl+Enter on Windows). Replies can be up to 5,000 characters. Add a photo On iPhone: tap the photo button next to the reply box, then Take photo or Choose from library. On the web: click the photo button at the left of the reply box and choose a photo or screenshot (up to 25 MB). Click the X to remove it before you send. You can send a photo with or without words. It stays in that topic, on the record, and can't be removed once it's sent.

s: Write what you need in plain words. Clearly gives it a short title and the right reply buttons.
k: new topic start post write duplicate
x: On iPhone On Topics, tap +, or tap New topic on Today. Write what you'd like to talk about. Tap Preview. Clearly shows how it will be sent: as a quick question, a question, an FYI or a conversation. Tap Post. On the web On Topics, click New topic. Say what you need. Click Post topic. If there's already a topic like it Clearly tells you when an open topic looks the same. You can add your message there as a reply, or post it as a new topic anyway. Start a topic about something specific From an event, an expense or a day on the calendar, use Ask about this. Clearly starts a topic that refers to it. Important: Posts can't be edited or deleted once they're posted. Read it through before you post.

t: When Clearly holds a message before it's sent
s: When a message is likely to make things harder, Clearly doesn't post it as written and suggests other wording. You choose what to send.
k: held not posted not sent as written rewrite suggested wording tone reframing
x: Clearly checks each message before your co-parent sees it. When a message is likely to make things harder between you, Clearly doesn't post it as written, and your co-parent doesn't see it. It says why, and suggests wording that keeps things moving. What you see Not posted as written (or Not sent as written for a reply), with the reason and a suggestion. Tap or click Use this wording to send the suggestion. Choose Edit my message to change it yourself and try again. Messages that were held aren't kept, and your co-parent never sees them. If you share the Messages paused for wording area with a professional, they see only a count over time, never the words. Get wording help before you send On iPhone, type your reply, tap Rewrite and choose Brief, Balanced or Warm. Set your usual style in Settings, then Reframing style. The suggestions are based on what you wrote and the conversation so far. You always decide what's sent.

t: When topics close on their own
s: Topics close after 30 days without activity, and proposals close after 30 days without an answer. Everything stays on the record.
k: auto close closes in inactive expired 30 days no activity no reply
x: So open topics don't pile up, Clearly closes them on its own. No activity for 30 days: the topic closes as Closed · no activity or Closed · no reply. You get a heads-up 2 days before. A proposal not accepted within 30 days: the topic closes as Closed · not accepted. The parent who hasn't answered gets a heads-up 3 days before. Any new message restarts the 30 days. In the last 7 days, the topic shows Closes in N days. Closed topics stay on the record, in full. To pick it up again, start a new topic.

t: Add, edit or delete an event
s: Add school events, appointments and activities to the shared calendar. Only the person who added an event can change it.
k: event appointment calendar repeat recurring delete event location
x: Add an event On iPhone: on Schedule, tap Add event. Enter the event name and an optional location. Pick one or more dates. Choose All day, or set start and end times. Under Repeat, choose Never, Daily, Weekly, Every 2 weeks or Monthly, with an end date or none. Choose which kids it's for, add notes if you like, and tap Create event. On the web: on Schedule, click Add event. Fill in the event, date and time. To repeat it, choose Daily, Weekly, Every 2 weeks or Monthly under Repeat, and an Until date. Add the location, kids and notes if you like, and click Add event. A repeating event with no end date is added for the next 6 months. Your co-parent is told once, about the whole series. Edit or delete Only the parent who added an event can edit or delete it. On iPhone: open the event, tap Event options, then Edit event or Delete event. On the web: open the day, then click Edit on the event. For a repeating event, choose this event only or this one and the ones after it. A deleted event comes off both calendars. Ask about an event Use Ask about this on an event to start a topic about it.

s: Choose the holidays you alternate, add your own, and set a different schedule for summer.
k: holidays summer christmas thanksgiving school break birthday alternate include weekend
x: Holidays On the web: go to Shared, then Custody schedule, then Edit holidays. On iPhone: go to Shared, then Plan, then Holidays. Switch between years with the arrows. Use the swap arrows on a holiday to change who has it that year. Holidays alternate each year. Turn on Include the weekend to add the weekend next to it. Add a holiday from the list, or add your own, such as a school break or a birthday, with its dates and who has it. Mark it as every year if the dates repeat. Stop tracking a holiday you don't alternate. The Holidays tab in the iPhone Schedule shows who has each holiday by year. Summer On the web: Edit summer. On iPhone: Shared, then Plan, then Summer schedule. Say whether summer is different from the rest of the year. Set when it starts and ends. Dates are kept as, for example, "the second Saturday in June", so they work every year. Choose a pattern: alternating weeks, alternating two weeks, alternating months, or extended time with one parent. Summer repeats every year until you change it. Note: A summer drawn day by day on iPhone is replaced if you save a pattern on the web. Clearly warns you before it does.

s: See each parent's share of parenting time for the month and the year so far.
k: parenting time overnights percentage time split totals
x: On the web, open Schedule and click any day. The day panel shows Parenting time for that month and overnights for the year, as counts and percentages for each of you. The totals follow the calendar as it stands, including holidays, summer and accepted swaps.

s: Ask to change days with your co-parent. They accept or decline, and an accepted swap updates the calendar for both of you.

Choose the day you'd like and, if you like, a day you'll give in return. Add a note and click Send request. Your co-parent is told. Answer a swap Open the request and choose Accept or Decline. Withdraw or undo To withdraw a request before it's answered, open it and choose Withdraw on the web, or •••, then Cancel request on iPhone. t: Set up or change your custody schedule

x: Patterns Week on / week off 2-2-3 5-2-2-5 3-4-4-3 Every other weekend Custom: draw your own, up to 4 weeks long On the web In the sidebar, go to Shared, then Custody schedule, and click Set up or Change. Choose a pattern. Say who has Week 1 (or who has the kids on the start date) and pick the start date. Set the exchange time. Check the four-week preview. Click a day to make its week Week 1. Then save. On iPhone Go to the Shared tab, then Plan, and tap Custody schedule. Choose a pattern and who starts. In the preview, tap a week to shift the schedule, or tap a day to choose which week is Week 1. Set the exchange time and tap Save. Good to know Either parent can change the schedule. The change shows for both of you straight away. Holidays and summer sit on top of the regular pattern. See Holidays and summer. For a one-off change, use a swap request instead. See Request or answer a swap.

t: See the schedule in Apple, Google or Outlook Calendar

On the web Go to Shared, then Calendar sharing. Click Turn on my calendar link. Click Add to Apple or Outlook or Add to Google Calendar, or Copy the link. On iPhone Open Settings, then Calendar sharing. Turn on Calendar feed. Tap Add to calendar, Copy link or Share link. Keep it private Anyone with your link can see the schedule. If you shared it by mistake, make a new link (Make a new link on the web, Generate new link on iPhone). The old one stops working. Your co-parent's link isn't affected. To stop it altogether, click Turn off on the web, or turn off Calendar feed on iPhone. Calendar apps refresh on their own schedule. Google Calendar can take up to a day. See The calendar link isn't updating.

s: Set the share each parent pays for the kids' costs, for all expenses or just one.

On iPhone: go to Shared, then Plan, then Shared expenses. Use the slider or a quick pick, or enter your share exactly. The new split applies to expenses logged from then on. Expenses already logged keep their split. For one expense When you log an expense, change the split for that one before you save it. On iPhone, tap Change. On the web, move the slider.

x: Only the parent who logged an expense can edit or delete it, and only while it's unpaid. On iPhone: open the expense, tap •••, then Edit expense or Delete expense. On the web: open the expense and use the edit or delete buttons. Once an expense is marked paid, it can't be changed. If you don't agree with an expense Use Ask about this on the expense to start a topic about it. The topic stays linked to it, on the record.

s: Add what it was for, the amount and a category. Clearly splits it using your agreed split, and your co-parent is told.

x: On iPhone On Expenses, tap Add expense, or use New expense on Today. Enter the amount and what it was for. Pick a category: Medical, Education, Sports, Clothing, Activities or Other. Check the split. It comes from your plan. Tap Change to use a different split for this expense only. Add a receipt photo if you have one. Save it. On the web On Expenses, click to log an expense. Fill in What it was for, Amount and Category. Adjust the split for this expense if you need to. Add a receipt (a photo or PDF) if you have one. Click Log expense. Your co-parent is told, and sees their share under Expenses. Tip: Set how you'd like to be paid back first, so your co-parent can pay you in one tap. See Set how you get paid back.

t: Pay your share or mark an expense paid

Tap or click Pay $X with Venmo (or PayPal, or Cash App). The app or site opens with the amount filled in. When you come back, Clearly asks whether you sent it. Choose Yes, and it's marked paid. If your co-parent prefers Zelle, cash or a check, the expense shows their details with a Copy button. Pay them, then mark it paid. Mark it paid Use Mark paid (iPhone) or Mark my $X paid (web). Your co-parent is told. If there's no way to pay shown, your co-parent hasn't said how they'd like to be paid back yet. Totals Expenses shows what you're owed and what you owe. On the web you can filter by Unpaid, Paid and Disputed.

Choose Venmo, PayPal, Cash App, Zelle, Cash or Check, and enter your details: Venmo: your username PayPal: your PayPal.me username Cash App: your $Cashtag Zelle: the email or phone number you use for Zelle On the web, a preview shows what your co-parent sees. t: Share the cost of Clearly through Expenses

To change it later: On the web: Settings, then Subscription, then Change or Stop sharing. On iPhone: Settings, then Subscription, then Sharing the cost. How it works You're still the one charged. Billing doesn't change. Each paid charge after that is added to Expenses as an unpaid expense, logged by you, at the split you chose. Your co-parent settles it the usual way. Changes apply from the next charge. Expenses already logged keep their split. Trials and free months never create an expense. If a charge is refunded, its expense is cancelled if it's still unpaid. Both parents can see whether the cost is shared. Only the parent who pays can change it. Note: This needs your co-parent to have joined, and works for US dollar subscriptions.

s: Doctors, the school, childcare, coaches and emergency contacts, in one list you both see.

To bring in contacts from your phone or another app, see Bring your calendar, contacts and records.

s: The custody schedule, holidays, summer, expense split, kids and contacts, kept the same for both of you.

x: Shared holds the parts of your parenting arrangement you both work from: The custody schedule, holidays and summer The expense split Your kids and their health details Contacts such as doctors, schools and coaches The family name Either parent can change any of it, and the change shows for both of you straight away. Until your co-parent joins, changes are free. After that, changes need the family's subscription. On the web, it's the Shared section of the sidebar. On iPhone, it's the Shared tab, with Plan, Kids and Contacts. The family name The family name shows at the top of Clearly and to any professional you share with. On the web, click Rename on a Shared page. On iPhone, open Settings, then Family, then Family name. Leave it empty and Clearly uses both parents' names.

s: Pick dates, a parent, keywords and what to include, then export a focused timeline as a PDF or CSV.

x: An exhibit is a timeline of just the entries you need, such as everything about school pickups since March. On the web Open Records and find Build an exhibit. Set From and To, choose Both parents or one parent, and add a keyword if you like. Choose what to include: messages, outcomes, schedule changes and expenses. Tick Only flagged entries to see only entries with a flag, such as no reply for 2 or more days, a resolution not accepted, a declined swap or a disputed expense. Click Build timeline, check it, then click Exhibit PDF or CSV. On iPhone Open Settings, then Export data, then Build an exhibit (PDF). Set the dates, who it was written by, and words it contains. Choose what to include, and whether to show flagged entries only. Tap Create exhibit (PDF). Flags are facts from the record. Clearly doesn't judge who was right.

s: Save one topic, with every reply and its times, as a PDF.

x: On iPhone: open the topic, tap ••• at the top right, then Export as PDF. On the web: open the topic and click Export this topic (PDF) in the side panel. The PDF includes every message as written, with the server times, and a document ID on every page.

t: Export your record as a PDF or spreadsheet
s: Download your full record, a single topic or a spreadsheet, for the last 30 days, 90 days or all time. Exports are always free.

Under For every PDF, choose Children's full names or Initials only, and optionally a state for the declaration. Choose what to download: - Full record (PDF): click Create PDF. - Spreadsheets: Topics, Expenses or Schedule & swaps as CSV files. On iPhone Open Settings, then Support, then Export data. Choose the record range, and how children are named in the PDF. Tap Full record (PDF), Build an exhibit (PDF) or All data (CSV). The file opens in the share sheet, so you can save it to Files, print it, or send it. What's in a PDF Every page carries a document ID, so anyone can check the PDF is genuine and unchanged. See Check a Clearly document. Note: Clearly keeps your record as it happened. Whether and how a record is used in court is a question for your lawyer.

x: On the web, Records has a From other apps section. Click Add a record to upload a PDF, image, CSV, text or Word file up to 25 MB, with its name, where it's from and the dates it covers. The file is kept exactly as you uploaded it. It's labeled Imported with its source, so it's never mistaken for something written in Clearly. It isn't turned into Clearly messages. Only the parent who uploaded it can remove it. Removing deletes it. Adding a record needs a subscription. Imported records are included when you share the Records area with a professional.

t: Check that a Clearly document is genuine
s: Every Clearly PDF has a document ID. Anyone can check it at getclearly.app/verify.

x: Every PDF Clearly makes has a document ID on every page. It looks like CLR-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX. To check one: Go to getclearly.app/verify. Enter the document ID from the PDF. Add the PDF when the page asks for it. Clearly compares the file with the one it made. If even one character was changed, it won't match. Anyone can check, without an account: your co-parent, a lawyer, a mediator or a court.

t: Change or end a professional's access
s: The parent who invited a professional can change what they see. Who can end access depends on their role.

x: Open Professionals (the sidebar on the web, Settings on iPhone) and find the professional under Who has access. Change what they see Use Change access (or Change what they can see on iPhone). Only the parent who invited them can do this. Your co-parent is told. End access Use End access, or Cancel invite for one they haven't accepted yet. Either parent can end access for these roles, because they work with both of you: Mediator Parenting coordinator Guardian ad litem Custody evaluator Only the parent who invited them can end access for these, because they're one parent's own: Family lawyer Therapist Coach Social worker Other professional After access ends They don't see anything new from that moment. They keep a read-only copy of your record as it was then, like a case file. Both parents are told. Access also ends on its own on the end date, if you set one. Both parents and the professional are told that day. An invitation nobody accepts within 30 days expires, and the parent who sent it is told.

t: Invite your lawyer, mediator or therapist

On iPhone: open Settings, then Professionals, then Invite a professional. Enter Their email. Choose their role: family lawyer, mediator, therapist, parenting coordinator, guardian ad litem, custody evaluator, social worker, coach or other professional. Under What they can see, check the areas. Clearly suggests areas for each role, and you can change them. Optionally set when Access ends. Leave it open to keep access until you end it. Add a note to them if you like, and send it. They get an email to create a free professional account, or sign in, and accept. Your co-parent is told When you invite a professional, your co-parent is told who and in what role. Both of you can see who has access and what they've viewed. Note: A professional uses a separate professional account. They can't use an email that belongs to a parent in Clearly.

Both parents see the same list. Past access shows professionals whose access has ended.

s: Only the areas you share, read-only, as you see them. Never your email, payment details or subscription.

x: You choose each area a professional can see: Topics: topics, replies, read receipts and resolutions. Messages paused for wording: a count over time of messages Clearly held back. Never the words, which aren't kept. Schedule: the parenting schedule, events and swap requests. Expenses: shared expenses, receipts and payments. Family info: children, contacts and places. Records: PDFs of the record, plus downloads of topics, expenses, the calendar and imported documents. Always private A professional sees parents by name only. They never see your email address, payment details, subscription or family code. They can't take part Professionals can't post, reply, answer, log or change anything. Nothing they do shows in your conversations.

t: When a professional invites you to Clearly
s: Set up your family first. Then you choose whether to share anything with them. A free month may be included.

x: If your lawyer, mediator or another professional invited you, their email has a Get started button. Tap Get started. If you already use Clearly, it signs you in. Set up your family, or join your co-parent's. Clearly asks whether to share with that professional. Tick the areas you're comfortable with, then: - Share read-only access to share now. - Not now to decide later. - No thanks to decline. They're told. Nothing is shared unless you say yes. If you share, your co-parent is told. A free month If the professional included a free month, it starts when your family is set up, whether or not you share. See A free month from a professional. Clearly never pays professionals for inviting families.

s: Open the link in the invitation email, sign in or create your account with the invited email, and accept.

The parent is told either way. You can also accept from the portal: invited cases are under the Invited tab in the sidebar. If it doesn't work "Sent to a different email address": sign in with the address the parent invited. "No longer open": invitations expire after 30 days. Ask the parent to send a new one. "Signed in with a parent account": sign out, and use a professional account. Both parents can see that you have access and what you view.

s: Family lawyers, mediators, therapists and parenting coordinators sign up free at web.getclearly.app/pro.

If a client invited you, use the email they invited. Choose your role: family lawyer, mediator, therapist, parenting coordinator, guardian ad litem, custody evaluator, social worker, coach or other professional. Add your firm or practice and your bar or license number if you like. Both are optional. Choose a password: at least 8 characters, with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a number. Agree to the terms and click Create free account. Confirm your email from the message Clearly sends, then sign in at web.getclearly.app/pro/login. You need a confirmed email before you can accept an invitation or invite a family. Separate from a parent account A professional account can't also be a parent account. If you're a co-parent in Clearly yourself, use a different email for your professional account. Note: Clearly doesn't check credentials. Families see the name, role and practice you enter.

x: Exports need the family to share the Records area with you. Open the case and go to Records. Choose Last 30 days, Last 90 days or All time. Choose children's full names or initials only, and a state for the declaration if needed. Download: - Full record (PDF), with a document ID on every page. - An exhibit: set dates and contents, click Build timeline, then Exhibit PDF or CSV. - Spreadsheets: topics, expenses, and schedule and swaps. - Documents the family imported from other apps. Inside a topic, Export this topic (PDF) saves just that topic. Each export is listed in the family's access log. Anyone can check a PDF at getclearly.app/verify.

t: How a client can invite you
s: A parent invites you from Professionals in their own app, with your email and role.

Tap Invite a professional, enter your email and role, choose the areas to share, and send it. You'll get an email with View the invitation. See Accept a parent's invitation. Your client's co-parent is told when you're invited, and both parents see who has access.

s: Email a parent an invitation from you, with the areas you'd like them to share and an optional free month.

x: On your Dashboard, click Invite a family. Enter the parent's email and, if you like, their name. Under What you'd like them to share, check the areas. Clearly suggests areas for your role. The parent can change them. Leave Include a free month of Clearly for them on, or turn it off. Add a short note if you like, such as "Ahead of our first session on Nov 12". Click Send invitation. The email comes from hello@getclearly.app, and replies go to you. If it doesn't arrive, ask them to check their spam folder. What happens next The parent sets up their family first. Then Clearly asks whether to share with you, and they choose the areas. Nothing is shared without their yes. If they share, their co-parent is told. The invitation shows as Shared with you once they do, and the case appears under Active. The free month 30 days of full access on the web and iPhone, no card needed, starting when they set up. It's a gift to the family, theirs whether or not they share. Clearly never pays professionals for referrals, and families are told so. s: Keep your own notes on a case. Only you see them.

x: Open a case and go to Private notes. Only you can see your notes. They're never shown to the parents or added to their record. You can save and delete notes. Your notes stay with you after your access ends.

s: Your profile, the families you invited, notifications and the getting-started guides.
k: settings profile notifications email for families phone sign out delete professional account
x: Open Settings in the sidebar. Profile: your name, role, practice, phone, bar or license number, and an Email for families if you'd like families to reach you somewhere other than your sign-in email. Families who share with you see your name, role, practice, email and phone. Families you invited: resend, edit, cancel or delete invitations. See Invite a family. Notifications: - Email me when a family changes what you can see or ends your access. Invitations are always emailed. - Choose which updates show on your Dashboard. Cases still show everything when you open them. Appearance: light, dark or automatic. Getting started: show the welcome steps again, take the tour, or bring back the sample family. Inviting clients: how a client can invite you from their own app. Account: Sign out and Delete my account. Delete your professional account Go to Settings, then Account, then Delete my account. Type DELETE and click Delete for good. Your access to every case ends straight away, and each family is told. Your private notes, case names and the copies of past cases you kept are deleted. Invitations you sent that haven't been answered are cancelled; a free month a family already started stays theirs. The families keep the record of what you viewed.

s: See what changed since your visit, the topics, schedule, expenses and records the family shared, read-only.

x: Open a case from your Dashboard or the sidebar. Overview What's new since your last visit: posts, topics closed, expenses logged, schedule changes and events added. Each shared area at a glance: open topics, the next exchange, unpaid and disputed totals. Patterns in the record: for each parent, typical reply time, topics waiting on them, resolutions proposed and accepted, schedule changes asked and answered, and expenses logged. These are counts from the record, not scores. Parenting time for the year so far, if the schedule is shared. Read-only You see the record exactly as the parents do. You can't post or change anything, and nothing you do appears in their conversation. Both parents can see what you open. Areas not shared An area the family didn't share shows with a lock. To see it, ask the parent who shared the case to turn it on. They do it from Professionals on the web, or Settings, then Professionals, on iPhone, then Change access. Your own name for a case Open the case menu and choose Rename case or matter no. to add your label and file number. Only you see them.

s: Find a case by name, parent or matter number, and search the words in shared topics.

Topics match words in topics and messages, in active cases that share Topics. Tick Include past cases to search the copies kept from cases that have ended. Note: When a search returns a family's messages, it's listed in that family's access log, with the words you searched. Both parents can see it.

t: Your dashboard and what needs a look
s: See which cases have updates, most urgent first, and go through them in one pass.
k: dashboard command center needs a look updates go through them attention
x: Your Dashboard shows every case, and the ones with something new. Needs a look Each case lists short updates, most urgent first: Expense disputed Resolution waiting: a proposed resolution hasn't been answered in 3 or more days. Waiting for a reply: a topic's last message is 2 or more days old. Schedule change: a swap is waiting, or was declined in the last 14 days. Unpaid expense: unpaid for 30 or more days. New posts: since your last visit. Access ending: within 14 days. These are dated facts with a link to the item. Clearly never scores a parent or draws conclusions. Go through them Click Go through them to open each case in turn. Each update ticks off when you open it. Click Next to move on, Finish at the end, or Stop at any time. Items you've seen stay hidden until they change. Your cases The table lists each case with its parents, last activity and access. Use the Active, Invited and Past tabs in the sidebar. In a case, press J or K (or ] and [) to move to the next or previous case.

s: The Taylors are a fictional family in every new account, so you can see how a case works before a real one arrives.

x: Every new professional account includes the Taylors, a fictional family, marked Sample. You're shown as Alex Taylor's family lawyer, with every area shared. A short tour shows what changed, messages exactly as written, and building an exhibit. Exhibits and PDFs work, and are marked as a sample. t: When your access to a case ends
s: Access ends when a parent ends it, the end date passes, or you leave. You keep a read-only copy up to that moment.
k: access ended past case leave case ask to share again archive end date
x: How access ends A parent ends it. For a mediator, parenting coordinator, guardian ad litem or custody evaluator, either parent can. For anyone else, only the parent who invited you can. The end date passes, if the parent set one. Access ending shows on your Dashboard 14 days before, and you and both parents are told on the day. You leave. Open the case menu and choose Leave case. Both parents are told. The parent who shared it leaves Clearly. If their co-parent stays, your access ends and you keep your copy, as below. If the whole family leaves Clearly, the family's record is deleted, including your copy. What you keep The case moves to Past. You keep a read-only copy of what you could see at that moment, and nothing after. You can still search it and build exhibits and spreadsheets from it. Your private notes stay with you. Ask to share again On a past case, Ask to share again lets the parents who shared it know you'd like access again. Nothing is shared unless a parent invites you again. You're emailed when a parent ends your access or changes what you can see, unless you turn that off in Settings.

s: Cancel on the web from Settings, or through Apple if you subscribed on iPhone. You keep access to the end of the paid period.
k: cancel stop subscription unsubscribe manage subscription apple subscriptions
x: Cancel where you subscribed. Only the parent who pays can cancel. If you subscribed on the web Sign in at web.getclearly.app. Go to Settings, then Subscription, and click Manage. Cancel on the page that opens. If you subscribed in the iPhone app Apple handles it: Open the iPhone Settings app. Tap your name, then Subscriptions, then Clearly. Tap Cancel Subscription. Or in Clearly: Settings, tap your subscription, Manage subscription, then Manage via App Store. Cancel at least 24 hours before the renewal date. After you cancel You and your co-parent keep full access to the end of the period you paid for. Then Clearly becomes read-only. Everything stays on the record, and you can still read, search and export it. Note: Deleting the Clearly app or your account doesn't cancel an App Store subscription. Cancel it with Apple first.

t: A free month from a professional
s: A professional's invitation can include 30 days of Clearly, free and with no card. It starts when your family is set up.

x: From a Clearly invitation If a professional invited you to Clearly with a free month: It's 30 days of full access, on the web and iPhone. No card is needed. It starts when your family is set up, whichever app you use, as long as you sign up with the email they invited. It's yours whether or not you share anything with them. It covers your co-parent too.
